trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or train to Kyoto (approx. 75 min from Osaka Itami or 2.5 hrs from Kansai International). Budget tip: Use IC card (Suica/ICOCA) loaded at the airport for cheaper transit fares.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Once settled, take a gentle evening-preview stroll through Maruyama Park — Japan's most famous hanami (cherry blossom viewing) park, likely in full bloom in mid-April. Admire the iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) and soak up the festive atmosphere. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the stone-lantern-lit lanes of Gion (Hanamikoji Street) at dusk for a magical first impression of Kyoto. Spot maiko (apprentice geisha) if lucky. Keep eyes open for the free Yasaka Shrine, beautifully illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab onigiri (rice balls) and green tea at a konbini (7-Eleven/FamilyMart) near the station — under ¥500.
meals.lunch: Grab a bento box or soba noodles at the airport or train station food court — budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Omen Noodle Restaurant near Gion — rustic udon with seasonal vegetables, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person. Family-friendly and casual.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light — jet lag is real! Purchase a 1-day or multi-day Kyoto City Bus pass (¥700/day) at the station for easy sightseeing from Day 2 onward. Load your IC card with ¥3,000–¥5,000 for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a peaceful early-morning walk through Maruyama Park before crowds arrive — cherry blossoms are stunning at sunrise. Head to Chion-in Temple (free outer grounds) and Shoren-in Temple (¥500 entry) for towering camphor trees and beautiful gardens. Kids will love the massive temple gates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (¥400 entry) — one of Japan's most iconic wooden stage temples with sweeping views over Kyoto. Walk down Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — charming preserved stone-paved lanes lined with craft shops and matcha cafes. Let kids try matcha soft-serve ice cream (¥350–¥500).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for a free self-guided walking tour. Visit Yasaka Shrine (free, open 24hrs). Enjoy the lantern glow along the canal at Shirakawa-minami-dori.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast near hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki, miso soup cup — under ¥600 per person.
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine set lunch at Tousuiro near Kiyomizudera — approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800. Vegetarian-friendly and great for families.
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market street food dinner — try tamagoyaki on a stick, fresh tofu, pickles, and skewers. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person for a satisfying market crawl meal.

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizudera can be crowded by 10am — aim to arrive at opening (6:00am) or after 3pm. Wear comfortable walking shoes — lots of stone steps. Strollers are difficult on Ninenzaka; baby carriers recommended for small children.

day_by_day.morning: Take Bus 205 to Fushimi Inari Taisha (free entry, open 24hrs) — the famous thousands-of-torii-gates shrine. Hike the lower loop (45–60 min) for families with young children, or push further up the mountain for quieter views. Cherry blossom trees line the lower trails in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Fushimi district for sake brewery culture. Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum (¥600 entry, includes sake tasting for adults) is educational and fun. Kids enjoy the historic brewery atmosphere and can sample amazake (non-alcoholic sweet rice drink). Walk along the scenic Fushimi canal lined with cherry trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining street parallel to the Kamo River. Enjoy riverside dining (kawayuka) if weather permits.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) — toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (kitsune-zushi) at a small shop near Fushimi Inari — the fox-shaped rice pouches are the local specialty, approx. ¥600–¥900.
meals.dinner: Budget ramen at Ippudo or local Kyoto ramen shop in Pontocho area — approx. ¥900–¥1,200 per person. Kids love ramen!

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is best visited early morning (before 8am) or late afternoon to avoid tour groups. The full mountain hike is 2–3 hours round trip and not recommended for very young children — the lower gates area is plenty rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by JR Miyakoji Rapid, ¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park — hundreds of free-roaming deer that bow for shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack). Kids absolutely love feeding the deer. Walk to Todai-ji Temple (¥600 entry) housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer area, ¥500 for inner treasure hall) with its famous stone and bronze lanterns. Stroll through Isuien Garden (¥900) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with Mount Wakakusa as a backdrop. Cherry blossoms frame the garden beautifully in April.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax in Maruyama Park — evening illuminations of the cherry blossoms are often held in April (free to view, check local listings for 2027 schedule).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or konbini breakfast — ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — Nara's regional specialty available at Hiraso restaurant near Todai-ji, approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya near Kyoto Station on the way back — filling family meal under ¥600 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a round-trip JR ticket to Nara at Kyoto Station. Do NOT use IC card for this route — buy a regular ticket for the cheapest fare. Keep small children close around the deer — they can headbutt for crackers! Bags with food should be held high.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Arashiyama district (30 min by bus or Randen tram from central Kyoto). Visit the iconic Bamboo Grove (free) — best before 8am for a crowd-free, mystical experience. Walk to Tenryu-ji Temple (¥500 garden entry) — a UNESCO World Heritage Zen garden with cherry blossoms reflected in the pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge and walk along the Oi River — gorgeous cherry blossom scenery. Visit Iwatayama Monkey Park (¥550 for adults, ¥250 for children) — a short hike up a hillside where wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids can feed monkeys from inside a cage (monkeys are outside — very unique!). Views over Kyoto are spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Take the scenic Randen tram back toward central Kyoto. Stop at Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen) for evening snacks and souvenir shopping — free to browse, snacks from ¥200.

meals.breakfast: Konbini or hotel breakfast — ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu hot pot) lunch at Sagano Tofu near Tenryu-ji — warming, healthy, and budget-friendly at ¥1,200–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki (Japanese savory pancake) at a DIY teppan restaurant in central Kyoto — fun for families, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Bamboo Grove is extremely photogenic but very crowded from 9am onward on weekdays and all day on weekends. Arashiyama is best done on a weekday morning. The Monkey Park hike is 15–20 min steep climb — manageable for most families but wear good shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Golden Pavilion — Kinkaku-ji (¥500 entry). Arrive at opening (9:00am) to beat crowds. The gold-leafed temple reflected in the mirror pond with cherry blossoms is one of Japan's most iconic images. Nearby Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) features Japan's most famous rock garden — great for a moment of calm and cultural reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nishijin Textile Center (free entry) — live kimono fashion shows (check schedule, usually 11am, 1pm, 3pm), weaving demonstrations, and hands-on textile crafts. Kids can try on mini-kimono for photos (small fee). Explore the Nishijin weaving district neighborhood — traditional machiya townhouses.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-michi) — a 2km canal-side path lined with hundreds of cherry trees. One of the most romantic and peaceful spots in Kyoto. End at Nanzen-ji Temple (free outer grounds) for evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local bakery — croissant and coffee, ¥500–¥700 (Western-style bakeries are common in Kyoto).
meals.lunch: Teishoku (set meal) at a local shokudo (casual diner) near Kinkaku-ji — rice, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Musashi Sushi near Nishiki Market — ¥130–¥200 per plate, great fun for kids, budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji is one of Kyoto's most visited spots — arrive right at 9am. The Philosopher's Path cherry blossoms may be slightly past peak by April 20 but still beautiful with petals falling (hanafubuki — cherry blossom snowstorm). Check bloom forecasts for 2027.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (15 min from Kyoto by Shinkansen/35 min by regular JR train, ¥580 one way). Visit Osaka Castle (¥600 castle tower entry, park is free) — cherry blossoms in the park may still be lingering. The castle museum inside is excellent for history lovers. Kids enjoy the castle towers and moat views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's famous neon-lit entertainment district. Walk across Dotonbori Bridge, see the iconic Glico running man sign, and explore the vibrant street food scene. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market (Osaka's Kitchen) for fresh seafood snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade (free to walk through) for budget souvenir hunting — 100-yen shops, anime goods, and fashion. Return to Kyoto by 9pm.

meals.breakfast: Konbini breakfast — ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Osaka street food lunch in Dotonbori — takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥600), kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers, ¥200/stick), and taiyaki (fish-shaped cake, ¥200). Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Okonomiyaki at Fukutaro in Namba — Osaka-style savory pancakes, the city's signature dish, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person. Kids love watching it cook on the teppan.

day_by_day.notes: Use JR Kyoto–Osaka line (not Shinkansen) for the cheapest fare (¥580 one way). IC card works on this route. Osaka is very walkable in the Dotonbori/Namba area. Keep an eye on children in the crowded Dotonbori area — it gets very busy in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore lesser-known Kyoto gems — start with Fushimi Momoyama Castle area (free exterior viewing) or visit Daigo-ji Temple (¥1,500 entry but includes 3 garden areas) — one of the best cherry blossom spots in Kyoto, historically famous for Toyotomi Hideyoshi's hanami party in 1598. Worth the splurge for blossom lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kyoto International Manga Museum (¥900 adults, ¥400 children) — 300,000 manga volumes you can read freely, interactive exhibits, and a lovely lawn where visitors read comics outdoors. Perfect for families and culture enthusiasts. Kids will be in heaven.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Teramachi and Shinkyogoku covered shopping arcades — budget souvenir shopping, 100-yen stores, snack shops, and traditional craft stores. Great for picking up omiyage (gifts) for people back home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or konbini — ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Soba noodle lunch at a traditional soba-ya near Daigo-ji — cold zaru soba with dipping sauce, approx. ¥900–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) at a local izakaya near Gion — casual, fun, and great for families. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person including soft drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Daigo-ji is a bit further from central Kyoto (take subway to Daigo Station, then 10-min walk) but is considered one of the top 5 cherry blossom spots in Japan. The three-story pagoda framed by blossoms is extraordinary. Check if blossoms are still active for late April 2027.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tofuku-ji Temple (¥600 garden entry) — famous for autumn foliage but equally beautiful with spring greenery and late cherry blossoms. The Hojo garden is a masterpiece of modern Zen design. Walk through the Tsutenkyo Bridge corridor for stunning garden views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Higashiyama Cultural District at a relaxed pace — Sanjusangendo Temple (¥600) houses 1,001 life-sized golden warrior statues (Kannon) — an awe-inspiring and slightly eerie experience that kids find fascinating. Walk to the Kyoto National Museum (¥700 general admission) for rotating cultural exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Gion — treat the family to a nicer sit-down dinner as a special occasion. Consider watching a traditional maiko performance at Gion Hatanaka (book in advance) or simply enjoy the magical lantern-lit streets one last time.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and miso soup from konbini — ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a local yoshoku (Western-influenced Japanese food) restaurant — a family favorite, approx. ¥800–¥1,200 per person.
meals.dinner: Special farewell Kyoto dinner — kaiseki-lite set menu at a mid-range restaurant (¥2,500–¥3,500 per person) OR splurge on a conveyor belt premium sushi bar. This is the one evening to treat yourselves.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to begin packing non-essentials and organizing luggage. Purchase any remaining souvenirs. Check train/transport options for departure day. Many temples offer early morning free access to outer grounds — worth a final sunrise walk through Maruyama Park.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk through Maruyama Park — say goodbye to the cherry blossoms. Visit Yasaka Shrine one last time (free, open 24hrs). Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at Nishiki Market (opens 9am) — matcha Kit-Kats, yatsuhashi (Kyoto's famous cinnamon sweets), and pickled vegetables make great gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel and store luggage at the hotel or at Kyoto Station coin lockers (¥400–¥700 depending on size). Take the train to the airport — allow 2–2.5 hours minimum before departure including check-in and security. Use remaining IC card balance on transit and last konbini snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, temples, deer, monkeys, street food, and the timeless magic of Kyoto.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast — visit a local kissaten for morning toast set or grab a proper ekiben (train station bento box) at Kyoto Station for the journey — ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Airport or train station meal — Kyoto Station has excellent budget food options on the basement and second floors including ramen, soba, and bento. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Return IC card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ¥220 handling fee) — only worth doing if significant balance remains. Keep 10-yen coins for temple donation boxes as a final cultural gesture. Kyoto Station has a great tax-free shopping area for last-minute purchases — bring your passport.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transit — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita/Haneda Express or Shinkansen toward Kyoto. Journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Freshen up and take a gentle first stroll through Maruyama Park to see the famous weeping cherry tree (Gion Shidare-zakura) illuminated in the late afternoon light. Soak in the hanami atmosphere as locals picnic beneath the blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — a short walk from Maruyama Park — lined with traditional wooden shops and lanterns. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab an onigiri and green tea at a convenience store (7-Eleven/Lawson) at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bento box at the Shinkansen station (Kyoto Station has excellent ekiben options for ¥800–¥1,200).
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles (Yasaka branch, 5-min walk from hotel) — a beloved Kyoto udon restaurant with a cozy atmosphere. Budget approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag will be a factor. The cherry blossom season in mid-April may be at late bloom or petal-fall stage; Maruyama Park's weeping cherry typically peaks slightly earlier, but the park remains beautiful. Confirm bloom status closer to travel.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Featured Experience) — Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to experience the park before crowds arrive. Admire the iconic weeping cherry tree, spread out a picnic mat, and enjoy a true hanami breakfast under the blossoms. Explore the adjacent Chion-in Temple and its massive sanmon gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Wagashi Making Class (Featured Experience) — Join a hands-on family workshop to craft wagashi, the beautiful Japanese sweets traditionally paired with matcha. Classes are typically 90 minutes and suitable for children. Conveniently located in the Gion/Higashiyama area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Gion district at dusk — the atmospheric heart of Kyoto's geisha culture. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and look out for maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to evening engagements. Browse souvenir shops for wagashi and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Picnic-style hanami breakfast — pick up onigiri, tamagoyaki, strawberries, and canned coffee/juice from a nearby convenience store or Nishiki Market. Budget ¥500–¥800 per person.
meals.lunch: Kagizen Yoshifusa — a historic Kyoto sweets shop near Gion with light lunch sets and matcha parfaits. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa — a friendly izakaya-style restaurant in Gion offering grilled skewers, tofu dishes, and Kyoto-style small plates. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Wagashi Making Class in advance as family slots fill quickly. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets. Children will love shaping the colorful wagashi sweets — great edible souvenirs!

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park (Featured Experience) — Take the city bus or Randen tram to Arashiyama (approx. 30–40 min from Gion). Walk through the ethereal bamboo grove early morning when light filters beautifully through the stalks. Then hike up Iwatayama Monkey Park (20-min uphill walk) where over 120 Japanese macaques roam freely — a huge hit with families!
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arashiyama further — visit Tenryu-ji Temple's stunning garden (UNESCO World Heritage Site), rent a rowboat on the Oi River, or browse the charming Togetsukyo Bridge area. Consider a short rickshaw ride through the bamboo lanes for a memorable family moment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto city center. Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for an early evening food walk — sample pickled vegetables, grilled skewers, fresh tofu, and tamagoyaki on sticks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) — try a morning set with toast, egg, and coffee for ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Shigetsu Restaurant inside Tenryu-ji Temple — a beautiful shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) experience with garden views. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,000 per person (splurge-worthy).
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market food stalls for a casual grazing dinner — budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person for various snacks and small bites.

day_by_day.notes: Monkey Park requires a small entrance fee (adults ¥550, children ¥250). Do NOT bring food in open hands near the monkeys. Start Arashiyama early (before 9 AM) on weekends to beat the crowds. Wear layers — mornings in April can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari Station (10 min). Hike the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates up the mountain. Go early to avoid crowds. Even a 30–45 minute hike partway up rewards families with stunning gate tunnels and city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by express train). Visit Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming sacred deer bow for deer crackers — an unmissable family experience. Walk to Todai-ji Temple to see the giant bronze Buddha (one of Japan's largest).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax with a soak in the hotel bath or visit a nearby sento (public bathhouse) for an authentic local experience.

meals.breakfast: Inari area convenience store or a small café near the shrine. Budget ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Kasugano Chaya near Nara Park — a casual restaurant serving kakinoha sushi (persimmon leaf-wrapped sushi), a Nara specialty. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person.
meals.dinner: Kyoto Gogyo — known for its signature burnt miso ramen, a comforting and unique Kyoto dish. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,600 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200) from vendors in Nara Park for the kids — the deer really do bow! Keep bags zipped as deer may nuzzle for snacks. JR Pass holders ride the Nara line for free.

day_by_day.morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) and Ryoan-ji Temple — Head northwest by bus. Marvel at the gold-leaf-covered pavilion reflected in the mirror pond — one of Japan's most iconic sights. Walk to nearby Ryoan-ji to contemplate the famous enigmatic rock garden, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishijin Textile Center — Learn about Kyoto's 1,200-year-old weaving tradition with live kimono fashion shows (free, held multiple times daily) and hands-on weaving demonstrations. Families can try on kimono for photos. Then visit Kitano Tenmangu Shrine, known for its plum and cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Pontocho Alley dinner — a narrow lantern-lit alley along the Kamo River, packed with atmospheric restaurants. Browse the menus and choose a spot that appeals to the family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Bibliotic Hello! in Nakagyo — a charming café with excellent coffee and pastries. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Tosuiro near Kinkaku-ji — a refined tofu cuisine restaurant in a traditional setting. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Pontocho restaurant of choice — look for set menus (teishoku) offering good value. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji is busiest mid-morning; arrive at opening (9:00 AM) for the best experience. The Nishijin Textile Center is free to enter and very family-friendly. Pontocho is best explored on foot — no cars allowed.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Kyoto → Tokyo by Shinkansen (approx. 2 hrs 15 min on the Nozomi). Check in to a mid-range hotel in Tokyo (recommend Shinjuku or Shibuya area for access to Day 6–10 activities). Drop luggage and head out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum (Featured Experience) — Immerse your family in a stunning world of interactive digital art installations. The museum (located in Azabudai Hills as of 2024 reopening) is a multi-room sensory wonderland — children and adults alike are captivated. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Azabudai Hills complex or head to nearby Roppongi for dinner. Alternatively, take the subway to Shibuya to witness the famous scramble crossing at night — a quintessential Tokyo moment.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kyoto or a quick stop at a Kyoto Station bakery (Sizuya is a beloved local chain). Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Ekiben (station bento) on the Shinkansen — a beloved Japanese travel tradition with regional specialties. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Gonpachi Nishi-Azabu — the atmospheric multi-level izakaya (inspiration for Kill Bill's fight scene) with excellent yakitori, noodles, and a fun ambiance for families. Budget ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Teamlab Borderless tickets online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. The Nozomi Shinkansen is the fastest option but requires a surcharge if using a JR Pass (use Hikari instead for full JR Pass coverage).

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (Featured Experience) — Explore Japan's most iconic food market with the whole family. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki on sticks, grilled scallops, fresh strawberries, and Japanese street food. Arrive by 8:00–9:00 AM for the freshest experience and smaller crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens — a short walk from Tsukiji, these beautiful traditional gardens feature cherry blossom trees (late petals possible in mid-April), a tidal pond, and a traditional tea house where you can enjoy matcha and wagashi. Then take a water bus (suijo bus) along the Sumida River to Asakusa for a scenic approach.
day_by_day.evening: Asakusa exploration — visit Senso-ji Temple beautifully lit at dusk, stroll Nakamise Shopping Street for souvenirs (ningyo-yaki cakes, folding fans, lucky charms), and enjoy the old-Tokyo shitamachi atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market grazing — fresh sushi breakfast, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person for a full market crawl.
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu Gardens tea house — light matcha set with seasonal wagashi. Budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person.
meals.dinner: Asakusa Imahan — a beloved sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji with a family-friendly atmosphere and excellent wagyu beef. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open daily but some stalls close on Wednesdays — check individual vendor schedules. The water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa costs approximately ¥800–¥1,000 per adult and is a wonderful scenic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Ueno Park and Museums — Ueno Park is one of Tokyo's top cherry blossom spots (late petals may still be visible in mid-April). Visit the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest, with incredible samurai armor, ukiyo-e prints, and ancient artifacts — very engaging for families). Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Akihabara Electric Town — a sensory overload of anime, gaming, electronics, and pop culture. Kids will love the multi-floor arcades (try crane games for prizes), Pokémon Center, and themed cafés. Then head to Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods, for a charming contrast — narrow lanes, artisan shops, and a historic cemetery.
day_by_day.evening: Shinjuku evening — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free entry, stunning night views of the city). Then explore the neon-lit streets of Shinjuku's entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby kissaten morning set. Budget ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Ueno Yabu Soba — a historic soba restaurant near Ueno Park serving handmade buckwheat noodles in a traditional setting. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho ('Memory Lane') — a tiny alley of yakitori stalls with smoky, atmospheric charm. Great for trying grilled skewers and cold Sapporo beer. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum has a dedicated children's corner and family audio guides. Akihabara arcades are entirely free to enter — just bring yen coins for games. The Metropolitan Government Building observation deck closes at 10:30 PM (last entry 10:00 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Shibuya and Harajuku — Start at Meiji Jingu Shrine, a serene forested Shinto shrine offering a peaceful morning contrast to the city. Walk through the forest to Harajuku's Takeshita Street — a colorful, quirky pedestrian lane beloved by kids (crepe shops, candy floss, character merchandise).
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya Sky Observation Deck — ascend to the open-air rooftop of Shibuya Scramble Square for 360-degree views of Tokyo (including Mt. Fuji on clear days). Afterward, explore the Shibuya Scramble crossing on foot and browse Tokyu Hands department store for unique Japanese goods and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba waterfront — take the Yurikamome monorail (a fun ride in itself, especially for kids) to the futuristic man-made island. See the life-size Gundam statue, enjoy the teamLab Planets (if tickets available), and admire the Rainbow Bridge illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Bread, Espresso & (Harajuku branch) — a beloved Tokyo bakery with excellent croissants, French toast, and coffee in a charming wooden house. Budget ¥900–¥1,400.
meals.lunch: Harajuku Marion Crepes — an iconic Harajuku experience; sweet crepes with endless topping combinations. Budget ¥600–¥900 per crepe.
meals.dinner: Odaiba Aqua City food court or Decks Tokyo Beach — wide variety of restaurants with harbor views. Try Ramen Republic (8 different ramen styles under one roof). Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance (especially for sunset slots which sell out fast). The Yurikamome monorail offers great views from the front car — arrive early to grab front seats. Teamlab Planets requires separate advance booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning at Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, with late-blooming cherry varieties (Ichiyo, Kanzan) that may still be in bloom in late April. Families can picnic on the lawns, explore the French formal garden, and visit the large greenhouse. A perfect, peaceful final Japan morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping and souvenir hunting — Shinjuku's Isetan department store basement (depachika) is a paradise for Japanese food gifts: matcha Kit-Kats, wagashi, regional snacks, and packaged ramen. Don't miss Don Quijote for affordable omiyage (souvenir) shopping. Head to the airport with plenty of time (allow 2–2.5 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Enjoy a final airport meal featuring a Japanese dish you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku Gyoen area — grab a morning bento or pastry from a nearby convenience store for a picnic inside the garden. Budget ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Nakamuraya Curry Restaurant in Shinjuku — a Tokyo institution since 1927, famous for its Indian-style curry with a Japanese twist. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent restaurant floors. Try a final bowl of tonkotsu ramen or a tempura set before boarding. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entrance fee (adults ¥500, children free). Alcohol is not permitted inside the garden. Leave sufficient time for airport check-in — Narita requires at least 2.5–3 hours, Haneda 2 hours. Use a luggage forwarding service (takuhaibin) if you've accumulated too many bags — available from your hotel.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the blooms, and enjoy traditional street food stalls (yatai) selling takoyaki and dango. A magical family-friendly cultural tradition that defines spring in Japan.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a stunning world of interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike are captivated by the light, sound, and motion experiences. A cutting-edge cultural attraction that blends technology with artistic expression unique to Japan.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Japan's most iconic food market with the whole family. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha soft serve, and grilled seafood skewers from dozens of vendors. A delicious deep dive into Japanese culinary culture that is approachable and exciting for all ages.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra fun.

experiences.name: Traditional Wagashi Making Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on family workshop to craft wagashi, the beautiful Japanese sweets traditionally served with matcha tea. Learn about the cultural significance of seasonal motifs — including cherry blossom designs — from a local artisan. Each family member creates and takes home their own edible artwork.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00; no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto. Settle into your suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Orientation Walk — After check-in, take a leisurely stroll through the historic Gion district. Admire the preserved machiya townhouses, spot maiko in traditional dress along Hanamikoji Street, and soak in the atmosphere of old Kyoto at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Night Viewing in Maruyama Park — Step directly from your hotel into Maruyama Park for an enchanting yozakura (night cherry blossom) experience. The iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) is dramatically illuminated after dark. Stroll the lantern-lit pathways and enjoy hanami in true Kyoto style.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or meal on board your flight.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, high-quality bite near Gion after check-in — try Omen Kodai-ji, a beloved Kyoto noodle restaurant steps from the park, for warming udon and seasonal vegetable sides.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten (Michelin 2-star kaiseki) — A short taxi ride from Maruyama Park, this legendary restaurant offers exquisite seasonal kaiseki cuisine celebrating spring ingredients. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. Confirm Kikunoi reservation before departure. Ask your hotel concierge about current peak bloom status upon arrival — timing may shift slightly year to year.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Daytime Hanami) — Begin the morning with a proper daytime hanami picnic beneath the famous weeping cherry tree. Your hotel concierge can arrange a premium bento picnic set with seasonal delicacies. Explore every corner of the park as the blossoms catch the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traditional Wagashi Making Class — Join a hands-on family workshop to craft wagashi, the beautiful Japanese sweets traditionally served with tea. Learn to mold nerikiri (sweet bean paste) into delicate cherry blossom shapes under the guidance of a master confectioner. Each family member brings home their edible creations.
day_by_day.evening: Kenninji Temple Evening Visit & Gion Dinner — Visit Kenninji, Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, just minutes from Gion, for a tranquil late-afternoon stroll through its rock gardens and painted fusuma screens. Then head into Gion for dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — your boutique stay likely offers a curated Japanese or Western breakfast; opt for the Japanese set with grilled fish, miso soup, pickles, and rice.
meals.lunch: Premium hanami bento picnic in Maruyama Park arranged by your hotel concierge, featuring seasonal Kyoto cuisine (obanzai) and local sweets.
meals.dinner: Mizai (Michelin 3-star kaiseki, Higashiyama) — An extraordinary multi-course kaiseki experience showcasing hyper-seasonal Kyoto ingredients. Intimate atmosphere perfect for a special family evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book the wagashi class in advance — family-friendly sessions fill quickly during cherry blossom season. Kenninji is free to walk around the exterior in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryuji Garden — Take a private car to Arashiyama (30 minutes from Gion). Walk through the iconic bamboo grove early in the morning before crowds arrive. Then explore the UNESCO-listed Tenryuji Temple and its stunning strolling garden with a backdrop of cherry blossoms and mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park — Hike up the forested hillside to Iwatayama Monkey Park, where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Feed them from inside a protected shelter while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below — a guaranteed family highlight. Return to Arashiyama village for browsing artisan shops along Togetsukyo Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Arashiyama Onsen Soak & Return — Before heading back, indulge in a private onsen bath at Hoshinoya Kyoto's riverside facility or a premium day-use onsen in Arashiyama. Return to Gion by private car for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Japanese breakfast set.
meals.lunch: Shoraian (Arashiyama) — A beautifully situated restaurant in a traditional villa offering tofu kaiseki cuisine; their yudofu (hot tofu) course is a Kyoto classic with stunning garden views.
meals.dinner: Kichisen (Arashiyama, Michelin 3-star) — If you can secure a reservation, this is one of Japan's most celebrated kaiseki restaurants, set in a traditional machiya. Alternatively, dine at your hotel's in-house restaurant for a relaxed evening.

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is very busy on weekends during cherry blossom season. Depart by 8:00 AM to enjoy the bamboo grove in relative peace. Private car hire is strongly recommended over public transport today.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Hike — Rise early for a private guided hike through the thousands of vermilion torii gates of Fushimi Inari Shrine (30 minutes south of Gion by private car). Hike as high as your family is comfortable — even the first 30 minutes reveal spectacular gate tunnels and mountain forest scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Pontocho Exploration — Return to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen'), a narrow covered arcade packed with premium Japanese food stalls. Sample pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, matcha confections, and grilled skewers. Browse Pontocho alley, one of Kyoto's most atmospheric dining lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Maiko Dinner Experience — Arrange through your hotel concierge a private ozashiki (maiko banquet) experience in a traditional Gion ochaya (teahouse). Watch a maiko performance, play traditional party games, and enjoy a formal kaiseki dinner in an authentic setting.

meals.breakfast: Early, light hotel breakfast before the Fushimi Inari hike.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market tasting walk — graze on premium street bites including fresh yuba (tofu skin), tamagoyaki, matcha soft serve, and seasonal pickles.
meals.dinner: Private ozashiki kaiseki dinner in a Gion ochaya — arranged exclusively through your concierge. This is a once-in-a-lifetime cultural dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: The ozashiki experience must be booked weeks or months in advance and is typically only accessible through hotel concierge connections or specialist agencies. Budget approximately ¥50,000–¥80,000 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path & Nanzenji Temple — Walk the iconic Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi), a canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees in full bloom, from Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion) south to Nanzenji Temple. The combination of blossoms, water reflections, and mountain backdrop is quintessential Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heian Shrine & Okazaki Cultural District — Visit the grand vermilion Heian Shrine and its expansive strolling garden, where late-blooming weeping cherries and wisteria create a stunning floral display. Explore the nearby Okazaki district's museums, including the Kyoto National Museum of Modern Art if cultural exhibits interest the family.
day_by_day.evening: Kaiseki Cooking Demonstration & Dinner — Book a private chef's table or cooking demonstration at a premium Kyoto restaurant, where a head chef walks your family through the art of seasonal kaiseki preparation before you sit down to enjoy the meal they helped inspire.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Omen (Nanzenji area) — A cozy, beloved noodle restaurant near the Philosopher's Path serving thick udon with seasonal vegetable sides; a local institution.
meals.dinner: Hyotei (Michelin 3-star, Okazaki) — One of Kyoto's oldest and most revered kaiseki restaurants, with a 450-year history. Their signature morning kaiseki and evening menus are extraordinary. Book months ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is best walked in the morning light. Wear comfortable shoes — today involves significant walking. Nanzenji's aqueduct and sub-temples (Nanzenin, Tenjuan) are worth the extra time.

day_by_day.morning: Bullet Train to Tokyo (Shinkansen) — Board the Nozomi Shinkansen from Kyoto Station (approx. 2h 15m to Tokyo). Travel first class (Gran Class) for the ultimate rail experience with complimentary meal service and wide reclining seats. Arrive at Tokyo Station and transfer by private car to your Tokyo luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Immerse your family in the world-famous teamLab Borderless, one of the world's most extraordinary digital art experiences. Hundreds of interactive, boundary-dissolving art installations spread across multiple rooms create a mesmerizing, ever-changing world that delights all ages. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba Waterfront & Dinner — Enjoy the futuristic Odaiba waterfront with views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline at dusk. Wind down with a premium dinner at a restaurant overlooking Tokyo Bay.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kyoto before departure.
meals.lunch: Gran Class bento on the Shinkansen — beautifully presented seasonal bento boxes served at your seat.
meals.dinner: Tableaux (Daikanyama) or Joël Robuchon (Ebisu) — For a family-friendly luxury experience, Joël Robuchon Tokyo offers an elegant French-Japanese fusion menu in a stunning château setting, perfect for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book Gran Class Shinkansen tickets well in advance. teamLab Borderless requires advance timed-entry tickets — purchase online before your trip. Confirm Tokyo hotel check-in time aligns with your arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Explore Japan's most iconic food market with a private guide. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, matcha products, and seasonal street bites. Learn the history of Tokyo's legendary fish market culture and interact with vendors who have run their stalls for generations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay Cruise — Walk through the beautiful Hamarikyu Gardens, a historic feudal garden with tidal ponds and late-blooming cherry trees, right next to Tsukiji. Board a traditional yakatabune (roofed pleasure boat) for a scenic cruise along the Sumida River, passing under cherry-blossom-lined bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza Luxury Shopping & Omakase Dinner — Explore Ginza, Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district, browsing flagship stores of Japanese and international luxury brands. End the evening with a world-class omakase sushi dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Market tasting — build your own premium meal from market stalls: fresh sea urchin, tuna sashimi, grilled oysters, and tamagoyaki.
meals.dinner: Saito (Ginza, Michelin 3-star omakase sushi) or Sushi Yoshitake (Ginza, Michelin 3-star) — intimate counter sushi with the finest seasonal fish. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji food tour is best started by 9:00 AM before the market gets crowded. The yakatabune cruise can be arranged through your hotel concierge and is particularly magical if cherry blossoms are still present along the Sumida River.

day_by_day.morning: Ueno Park Cherry Blossoms & Museums — Visit Ueno Park, Tokyo's most famous hanami spot, for a morning stroll under the cherry trees (late blooms may still be present). Explore the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's oldest and largest museum — with its extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ancient ceramics, and Buddhist art. A private guided tour is recommended for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Asakusa & Senso-ji Temple — Walk through the historic Asakusa district to Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest and most dramatic Buddhist temple. Stroll the Nakamise shopping street for premium Japanese crafts, fans, and traditional snacks. Explore the backstreets of Yanaka, Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree Sunset & Dinner — Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) for panoramic sunset views across the entire Kanto region. On a clear evening, Mt. Fuji is visible on the horizon. Dine at the tower's premium restaurant or in nearby Asakusa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Sometaro (Asakusa) — A charming, historic okonomiyaki restaurant where you cook your own savory pancakes at the table; a fun, interactive family lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Hommage (Asakusa, Michelin 1-star) — A creative French-Japanese restaurant by Chef Atsushi Tanaka, offering an inventive tasting menu that blends classical French technique with Japanese ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tokyo National Museum private guided tour in advance. The Skytree observation deck tickets should be pre-purchased online to avoid long queues. Check cherry blossom status in Ueno — late April may see green leaves beginning to appear.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nikko (Private Car) — Journey by private luxury car (approx. 2 hours) to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Nikko, home to the extraordinarily ornate Toshogu Shrine complex. A private guide brings to life the history of the Tokugawa shogunate through the shrine's intricate carvings, gilded gates, and cedar-forested mountain setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nikko National Park & Kegon Falls — Explore the natural splendor of Nikko National Park. Visit the thundering Kegon Falls (97m), one of Japan's three great waterfalls, and take a glass elevator to the observation platform at the base. Stroll along the shores of Lake Chuzenji surrounded by mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo & Farewell Dinner — Return to Tokyo by private car. Enjoy a relaxed, celebratory farewell dinner at one of Tokyo's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Meiji-no-Yakata (Nikko) — A beautifully restored Meiji-era Western-style villa serving elegant European cuisine in a forest garden setting; a historic and atmospheric lunch stop.
meals.dinner: Quintessence (Shirokanedai, Michelin 3-star) — Chef Kishida's extraordinary French fine dining experience, widely considered one of Tokyo's absolute best. A perfect celebratory finale.

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is best explored with a private guide who can provide context for the complex iconography of Toshogu. The mountain roads to Lake Chuzenji involve a winding hairpin route (Irohazaka) — some family members prone to motion sickness should take precautions.

day_by_day.morning: Harajuku & Omotesando Morning — Explore the tree-lined Omotesando boulevard (Tokyo's Champs-Élysées) for luxury boutique shopping and architecture. Visit Omotesando Hills and the flagship stores of Japanese designers. Stroll through Harajuku's Takeshita Street for a colorful contrast — a fun cultural experience for younger family members.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shibuya & Teamlab Planets (Optional) — Visit the iconic Shibuya Crossing, the world's busiest pedestrian intersection, and explore the area. If the family wishes to experience more digital art, teamLab Planets in Toyosu offers a different, water-based immersive art experience. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxing afternoon at your hotel spa before departure preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Airport Transfer — Private luxury transfer to the airport. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport's premium restaurant lounges, or arrange an early dinner near the hotel before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor every bite of the Japanese breakfast set.
meals.lunch: Maisen (Omotesando) — Tokyo's most celebrated tonkatsu restaurant, serving perfectly breaded, premium Kurobuta pork cutlets in a beautifully converted bathhouse. A beloved Tokyo institution.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at ANA Suite Lounge or JAL First Class Lounge (if applicable), or a final dinner at Narita/Haneda's premium restaurant options before your flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in and security. If your flight departs late evening, you have ample time for a full afternoon of activities. Ask your hotel concierge to arrange luggage forwarding (takkyubin) to the airport the day before so you can explore freely on your final day.
